catalog_quote: 1.3 Stress Word stress in Seko Padang is penultimate. 1.4 Echo Vowel Free standing words don't end in /k/ in SP, although they do in Seko Tengah. SP has innovated an echo vowel which attaches to the underlying /k/-final root. Also note the placement of stress in the following examples. (3) /ba`hulaka/ 'hair (of one's head)' /ma-`rèreke/ 'ADJ-deserted' /`lantiki/ 'ant' /`osoko/ ... /`tannuku/ 'horn' This is the pattern that emerges in (3): a. The last two vowels are identical. b. There is antepenultimate stress; irregular for SP. Interestingly, the echo vowel is retained when adding a possessive suffix (4). Stress becomes penultimate. (4) /bahula`ka-mu/ 'your hair' /oso`ko-ku/ 'my side' /tannu`ku-na/ 'its horn' ... 2.1 Examples With Long Vowels Stress is on the first syllable in all of the following words. (5) [mata] 'eye' [mata:] 'raw' [mate] 'dead' [ate:] 'liver' [sali] 'floor' [pali:] 'widow(er)' [màlo] 'dry' [hàlo:] 'hole' [hulu] 'body hair' [hulu:] 'shin' ... [2.2.1] If we were to interpret the long vowels in (5) as sequences of two vowels, we would need to account for the antepenultimate stress. From that standpoint it seems best to treat the long vowels as having a single syllable peak.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the word. Word-final contrastive long vowels (mata: 'raw') count as a single syllable peak, so stress stays on the penult. Possessive suffixes (-ku, -mu, -na) and nominalizing -ang are stress-shifting (stress moves rightward to stay penultimate). The only stated irregularity: roots with an underlying final /k/ take a word-final echo vowel that does not count for stress, giving surface antepenultimate stress (ba-hulaka, tannuku); with a possessive suffix added these revert to penultimate.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said about secondary stress in either Laskowske 1991 or 2006.
new_statements.exceptions: Echo-vowel words (underlying /k/-final roots, e.g. /ba-hulaka/ 'hair', /tannuku/ 'horn') have antepenultimate stress, explicitly called 'irregular for SP'; the echo vowel -i/-V is non-stress-shifting (Laskowske 2006 sec. 2.3). Final long vowels do not attract stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Stated for the word ('word stress'), illustrated on citation forms of roots and on suffixed words (possessives, nominalizations); stress-shifting suffixes show the domain includes suffixes. Laskowske 2006 (10-ICAL, sec. 2.1 item 7, p.3) restates 'Stress is penultimate.' as a feature common to all four Seko languages, with Seko Padang examples.
new_statements.identity_note: Laskowske 1991 describes Seko Padang proper (fieldwork from 1984 in the homeland; principal dialect Hono' [= Wono], minor dialect Lodang; no dialect restriction stated for the stress rule). Laskowske 2006 states the same penultimate rule as common to the whole Seko subgroup (Seko Padang seko1243, Seko Tengah seko1244(?)/[sko], Panasuan [psn], Budong-Budong budo1241) with Seko Padang examples.

sources.note: Sec. 1.3 (p.2): 'Word stress in Seko Padang is penultimate.' Sec. 1.4 (p.3): words with the innovated echo vowel after an underlying /k/-final root (/ba-hulaka/, /tannuku/) have antepenultimate stress, 'irregular for SP'; adding a possessive suffix makes stress penultimate again. Sec. 2.1-2.2.1: final long vowels (mata: 'raw') keep stress on the first syllable, so long vowels are analysed as single syllable peaks ('Word Stress Remains Penultimate'). Sec. 3: contrastive quick vowels only in stressed syllables.

sources.note: Deciding sentence: word stress is penultimate (sec. 1.3). Exceptions stated: (i) echo-vowel words built on underlying /k/-final roots, e.g. /ba-hulaka/ 'hair', /tannuku/ 'horn', carry antepenultimate stress, 'irregular for SP'; stress returns to penultimate when a possessive suffix is added (/tannu-ku-na/). (ii) Word-final contrastive long vowels ([mata:] 'raw', [ate:] 'liver') are stressed on the first syllable of a disyllable; the author treats the long vowel as a single syllable peak so that stress stays penultimate (sec. 2.2.1 'Word Stress Remains Penultimate').
